content:
1 year ago I got called to something I wasn’t ready for. Sometimes the things your called to isn’t what you want but it’s what you need. 

It’s been an amazing year meeting and connecting with people on a deeper level and discussing the teachings of Jesus. 

LaVida 1%ers

Every visionary needs a integrater and the integrater needs a vision. 

More importantly every partnership needs to be built in trust and aligned values. We go farther together. 

Grateful for my friend, brother and business partner. @itisdrey 

Most

The one who has been by my side for 32 years straight. Big Happy Birthday Mom! 

There are  not many people that will stick by you and love you for that long. Grateful 🙏

I was banging my head against the wall teaching a job I didn't love, drinking more than I should have, until my grandfather pushed me toward a commercial that changed everything. I believe the breaking point is usually the opening, you just have to be honest enough to walk through it. Who pushed you toward your turning point?

AI can write your emails. It cannot sit across from you at dinner and ask how you're really doing.

I feel overstimulated most days, on a screen all day, talking to bots instead of people, using AI every single day in business. I still eat dinner alone more than I'd like to admit, even though I'm a well connected guy with a lot of friends. That's me not being intentional.

Here's what I believe is coming. As AI keeps growing, human connection is going to be in higher demand than it has ever been in our lifetime. People are going to want real conversations, walks, dinners, actual time together, because a robot can say the right words and still never actually see you.

So here are three ways to build that connection starting today.

Compliment people out loud instead of just thinking it. Make it growth based when you can, something like "you're the hardest worker I know" instead of just "you're smart," because growth based compliments actually help people become more of who they're trying to be.

Host something, a dinner, a coffee, one person over to your place. Hosting makes you the connector, and people remember who brought them together.

Reach out when someone crosses your mind. A voice note, a quick video, a text that says "thinking about you." Most people are walking around not feeling seen at all, and that one message changes someone's whole day.

Use AI to automate what you don't want to do, then spend the time you bought on the people you love. That's the whole point of having more capacity.

If you're building alone right now and craving people who get it, that's exactly why we built the Owners Club. Drop "club" below and I'll send you the details.

I used to think I wasn't smart enough to be a business owner. It was a lie that I picked up. It was rooted in something that happened to me in second grade, and it followed me for years without me even knowing it was there. Go back to when you were 12 years old and ask yourself what you were really dealing with. You might find the thing that's been running the show the whole time.

You will believe whatever story you keep telling yourself over and over again, even if it's a lie, and comfort is one of the loudest lies out there. It tells you you're fine right where you are. Do you actually believe that, or does some part of you already know you're due for a change?

Nights like these are the ones we all love. Shaking hands with brothers, having real conversations with sisters and being in a room of high energy of business owners who are building something real and impactful. 

The 1BB Owners Club isn't just another app or another group. It's a special room with special people. It's where we think bigger and grow faster. 

If you want to start to growing your online presence and authority while also building along side other motivated and inspired founders. DM me Owner.

That message has been drilled into me, and it's why I built this instead of grinding it out solo. 1BB is bigger than me, it's a family of killers who want to be free, high values, great character, and God. If you're building alone right now, you don't have to do it like this.

If I could impose one rule on everybody, that would be it. Everyone is listening to everything everybody else tells them, and almost nobody stops to think for themselves anymore. Tag someone who needs to hear this before they let the noise make another decision for them.

I'll use AI to automate the stuff I don't want to do, but I'm never letting it replace real conversations with real people. People are going to keep gravitating toward exceptional experiences and real human connection, especially while everyone else is handing it over to the bots. We have built an Owners Club for founders who know the value in real relationships not only for the business but their personal growth. The right people are more valuable than the next ai prompt.

Last night I hosted a Bible study with 8 people in the room, no phones out, just real talk about life, and I walked out feeling better than I have in weeks. You cannot get that from a screen, no matter how good the bot gets at sounding like it cares.

Here are three things I want you to try this week, and none of them cost you a dime. First, give someone a growth based compliment instead of a looks based one, something like telling them they're generous or that they work harder than anyone you know, because that gives them something they can actually build on. Second, host something small, a dinner, a coffee, a walk, because the person who brings people together is the person everyone starts gravitating toward. Third, reach out to someone just because they crossed your mind, not because you need anything from them, just a text or a voice note letting them know you were thinking about them. 

People want this so badly right now, they're just out of practice at it. Everyone's eating dinner alone, scrolling instead of calling, and nobody wants to be the first one to suggest hanging out because it feels a little weird now. That's exactly why it works when you do it anyway.

Pick one person today and reach out to them. You can be the one who starts it. Let's go.

My vision keeps growing and so does the weight that comes with it, but I'm not carrying it by white knuckling control. I surrender to God so I can actually keep my peace while I build. If you're trying to hold every piece of your business together by yourself, this is your reminder that you don't have to.

Asking better questions. Getting better answers 💪

Surrounded by great people. Motivated to create more impact. 

Life is a gift. Let's keep growing. 🔥

I get tired of eating dinner by myself, and I think a lot of us are starving for the same thing without saying it out loud. Breaking bread with somebody, having a real conversation, that's what we're meant to do, not idolizing status and money while we isolate ourselves. Who's someone you need to call and set up dinner with this week?

So here's what took me forever to figure out. You can walk into any room, shake any hand, feel confident in your career, your relationships, all of it, and still not believe you're worthy of what you're chasing. That's not a confidence problem. That's a self-esteem problem. Have you ever caught yourself sabotaging something good and couldn't figure out why?

Your brain decides what's "cheap" based on what it saw first. It's called anchoring.

I went car shopping with a $30k budget. My friend showed me a $75k car first, and I fell in love with it. Then he showed me a $40k car, and my brain immediately said, "yo, that's a steal." The $40k car hadn't changed. My reference point had.

That's anchoring. Whatever number someone sees first becomes the measuring stick for everything after it. Swipe to see how this works in real life 👇

I'm not built to shrink down and take a seat when some version of me whispers to slow down. The part of me that's powerful, complex, ten layers deep doesn't need more strategy, it needs permission to exhale and release. I believe the version of you that's regulated and grounded will always outwork the version running on stress and discipline.

Everybody wants to plan the trip a year in advance and I just don't get it. I don't know who I'm gonna be next week, let alone next year, so I'm not committing to a version of me that doesn't exist yet. If you're growing the way I plan on growing, how do you plan a year ahead with someone you might not even like by the time you get there?

Everyone's talking about keeping up with AI and nobody's talking about what it's doing to your nervous system. I'm using it every day in business and I still make time to close the laptop, open a notebook, and just breathe. That quiet hour isn't laziness, it's how you stay a human being in a world that's forgetting how.
